Electrification of steam cracking as a pathway to reduce the impact of the petrochemical industry on climate change. Journal of Cleaner Production 427, 139208. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jclepro.2023.139208. Supplementary material mmc1 (docx, SM1-SM7) and mmc2 (xlsx, SM8).

Locators: printed page numbers = PDF pages (13 pp.); SI locators name the supplement section (SI file mynko_2023_steam-cracking-electrification-si_jclepro.docx/.xlsx). A cradle-to-gate LCA on first-principles simulation (COILSIM1D, Petro-SIM) of one propane steam-cracking furnace (10 t/h propane to the coil, 85% conversion) with its share of a demethanizer-first separation train; European scope, Belgian/EU/NL/NO grids as sensitivities. Main file: six cases from Table 2 (p.8) and the SI SM5 energy-flow table - BASE fired tubular cracker, low-emission furnace with electrified compressors (L-E), L-E with air preheater, RotoDynamic reactor (RDR), hydrogen-fired furnaces with integrated SMR+CCS and GHR/ATR+CCS - all per t ethylene (hourly flows / ethylene kg, no allocation to the other HVCs; HVC masses in _flows and _other-values allow rebasing). Fired duty = radiant-box heat released; auxiliary-boiler natural gas = printed duty / printed 93% boiler efficiency; RDR preheater fuel = printed duty / printed 88%; CO2 = furnace (Table 2) + auxiliary boiler (SM5). Plus the reprinted typical propane plant (621 MW fired for 125 t/h ethylene; Zimmermann and Walzl 2009). Flows: propane, internal fuel gas, fuel-gas and steam exports, HVC co-products, ASU oxygen. Other-values: LCA climate change per kg HVC for all 15 case-grid combinations, grid intensities, breakevens, yields, efficiencies. Not loaded: other 15 LCA impact categories, chart-only results (Figs 7-11), reformer stream tables, hydrogen prices. No costs (second-order LCA, capital goods omitted).
